newsitem.title: TURKEY: Moslem businessmen protest over Turkish haj policy.
newsitem.headline: Moslem businessmen protest over Turkish haj policy.

text.p: Islamist businessmen complained on Monday that the Turkish state's control of the annual Moslem pilgrimage to Mecca violated the rights of believers.

"The way the state now organises the haj pilgrimage violates constitutional law, human rights and freedom of choice," Ali Riza Demircan of the Independent Industrialist and Businessmen's Association (MUSIAD) told a news conference.

Demircan, head of the Islamist group's tourism section, said its 25 member travel agencies were deprived of the chance to take a slice of more than $100 million in annual haj revenues because they failed to meet the state's strict regulations.
Saudi Arabia has set an annual quota of 60,000 pilgrims from Turkey, who last year paid $1,900 each for state-run tours.

Islamists, their influence boosted since Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan took office this year, have vowed to push down the cost of pilgrimages by reviving overseas and overland routes through Syria and Jordan.

The Tourism Ministry, controlled by Erbakan's Islamist Welfare Party, supports the use of such routes but the Interior Ministry and religious affairs office, led by the conservative wing of the coalition, oppose using them.
Since the Gulf War in 1991, pilgrims have been forced to fly to Saudi Arabia and have to apply for tickets six months in advance.

Authorities in Turkey, which is secular but 99 percent Moslem, limit the tours to companies with several years' experience and sizeable annual sales. Travel agencies running the tours receive 20 percent of revenues.
Demircan said the state's Directorate General of Religious Affairs took another 25 percent of the income.
"They have formed a monopoly in the sector, it means the mafia dimension of the state has won," Demircan said.
